definition: Owner-settled 2026-10-15. Eligibility: devices most sold, most used, and still in rotation. Ranking: user demand — what needs the most help to let users fix their devices first. Scope: any device people genuinely need (kitchen appliances, washers and dryers, baby monitors — not gadgets only).

scoring.demand: Users needing repair per year (installed base x failure rate; repair-seeking demand), log-scaled: 10 = >=50M/yr, 9 = ~10M, 8 = ~5M, 7 = ~1M, 6 = ~500k, 5 = ~100k.
scoring.consequence: Documented downtime consequence. Anchors: 10 = injury/stranded/missed medical care; 8 = lost work + major daily function; 7 = food loss $300-$1,200; 6 = hygiene/safety-adjacent; 5 = major inconvenience; 4 = workaround exists; 3 = entertainment; 2 = minimal.
scoring.lockout: Owner-repair blockage: repairability scores, parts availability (Open Repair Alliance #1 barrier at 25%), parts pairing, proprietary tools, sealed construction.
scoring.sensitivity: Product form (Demand x Consequence x Lockout) ranks identically at the top: powered wheelchair ~700, smartphone ~490 — the conclusion is not weight-sensitive.

dilemma_conclusion: The evidence puts powered wheelchairs ABOVE phones on the user-demand composite (UDS 8.8 vs 8.15): wheelchairs carry the maximum consequence (62% of surveyed users report 4+ week repair waits; stranded, stuck in bed, repairs suffer adverse consequences — 27.6%-66% across four verified studies, each counting a different population, ADJUDICATED with exact citations — (dealer-gated programming tools, proprietary buses, configuration locked in the controller, no public schematics for many models). On raw demand volume, phones lead by ~20-30x (~29M US repairs/yr vs ~1M wheelchair service-needing users/yr) — shown honestly. Washers do NOT rank above phones on the composite (5.3 vs 8.15): their demand volume is comparable but consequence and lockout are low — the owner-fix path already exists. Under the owner's definition — what needs the most help to let users fix their devices first — the wheelchair is the top entry: it is the device users most need help fixing and the one where the path does not exist.

Removed the 7 lowest-UDS entries to keep the list at 100: HackRF One, RTL-SDR Blog V3, Flipper Zero, ClockworkPi uConsole, Valve Index, Playdate, Steam Deck OLED (all remain documented in the W³ bench materials and the site archive). devices.name: Powered Wheelchair

sources.note: US PIRG — wheelchair repair survey and right-to-repair law
Archives of PM&R 2024 — wheelchair repair delays and adverse outcomes

devices.why: Users' legs, replaced: when the electronics fail, the user is stranded — and today the fix path runs through dealer-gated tools.
devices.usage_evidence: 5.5-6M people in the US use wheelchairs (>2% of adults; GoodRx/Medicare, 2026); the powered subset is not precisely published — category-scale. 93% of wheelchair users needed service in the preceding year; 68% needed 2+ repairs (US PIRG 2022).

repair_guide.label: iFixit
repair_guide.note: iFixit device-class repair hub: repair guides and troubleshooting for this class of device, with model pages linked from it. Verified live 2026-10-15 (HTTP 200, exact device title).

user_demand_score.demand_evidence: 5.5-6M US wheelchair users (GoodRx/Medicare, 2026); 93% of users needed service in the preceding year and 68% needed 2+ repairs (US PIRG 2022 survey) — roughly 1M+ service-needing users/yr, powered subset category-scale.
user_demand_score.consequence_evidence: 62% of surveyed wheelchair users (87 of 141) reported average repair waits of 4+ weeks (US PIRG 2024 survey). Adverse consequences among users needing repairs — ADJUDICATED, verified across four studies, each counting a different population: 27.6% (104/377; Toro, Worobey, Boninger, Cooper & Pearlman, Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2016;97(10):1753-60 — people with SCI who needed >=1 repair, mixed manual/power); 42% (127/310; Worobey et al., Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2022;103:779-89 — SCI Model Systems participants reporting repairs); 43.5% (Henderson, Boninger, Dicianno & Worobey, Disabil Rehabil Assist Technol 2022;17(3):331-337 — veteran wheelchair users experiencing repairs); 66% (Worobey et al., Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2025;106(3):379-86, online Oct 2024 — FULL-TIME users >=40h/wk with >=1 repair in prior 6 months; median repair time 14 days; vendor repairs produced more consequences than self/family). VA audit found 69-day average waits. Individuals with consequences have 1.73x odds of pressure injuries and 1.81x odds of rehospitalization (Hogaboom et al. 2018, cited in Worobey 2025).
user_demand_score.lockout_evidence: Controller configuration requires dealer-gated software/handheld programmer (LiNX: 'software provided by the controller manufacturer'); proprietary buses (R-net, LiNX, Curtis); firmware bin files require a dealer license (practitioner accounts); manufacturers publish no schematics for many models (some publish service manuals — Sunrise QM-7, Invacare Pronto M41 — access inconsistent); NO cryptographic parts pairing — the gate is tool and configuration access.

mission_test.path_exists: PARTIAL — mechanical and battery work exists; electronics do not.
mission_test.tools: Order a replacement battery or joystick module and connect it — batteries are user-replaceable on many chairs. For controller/power-module faults: none — the configuration and firmware require dealer-gated software or a handheld programmer (LiNX/R-net/Curtis), and firmware downloads need a dealer license.
mission_test.blocks: Proprietary buses (R-net, LiNX, Curtis); dealer-gated programming software, handheld programmers and firmware files; configuration locked in the controller; no public schematics for many models (some manufacturers publish service manuals — access inconsistent); the repair market is a duopoly (Numotion, National Seating & Mobility) with 4-7 week waits.
mission_test.what_would_change_it: Manufacturers publishing schematics/service manuals for power modules and controllers, bus protocol documentation (R-net/LiNX/Curtis), programmer tool access or open-source alternatives, and configuration/calibration procedures. The Wheelchair Right to Repair Act (introduced in Congress, Aug 2025) would require exactly this; Colorado, Nevada, Oregon and Washington have passed state laws.

methodology: Owner-settled 2026-10-15. Eligibility: devices most sold, most used, and still in rotation. Ranking: user demand — what needs the most help to let users fix their devices first.
